anatomy.intro: Four structures that explain the form of the probable peanut cactus hybrid.

parts.function: The green succulent stem stores water and captures light.
parts.label: Finger-shaped stem

parts.function: Longitudinal folds organize the expanding stem surface.
parts.label: Shallow rib

parts.function: Small cushions carry neat clusters of short spines.
parts.label: Areole

parts.function: A young side shoot helps the plant spread into a low clump.
parts.label: Basal offset

flowers.text: The peanut-cactus ancestor has vivid red flowers about 5–7 cm across. Hybrid flowers can differ, so this plant's first clearly documented bloom will be more informative than a guessed cultivar name.

growth.note: These expectations come from peanut-cactus ancestry; a hybrid can differ in vigor, stem size, and flower color.

stages.text: Short stems establish a compact starting group.
stages.title: Small cluster

stages.text: New fingers enlarge the plant sideways.
stages.title: Spreading offsets

stages.text: Mature stems can bear flowers much broader than the stems themselves.
stages.title: Flowering clump

habitat.text: Chamaelobivia is a horticultural hybrid group, not a wild species with one native range. Its peanut-cactus ancestor, Echinopsis chamaecereus, comes from northwestern Argentina. This plant's low cluster of finger-shaped stems supports the hybrid-group identification, but its exact parentage and cultivar remain unknown.

No flowers, grafts, or roots. Numbers must remain readable at 350px. Generic anatomical specimen, not measurement evidence. Probable Chamaelobivia peanut cactus hybrid: dense low cluster of short finger/peanut-shaped bright green stems, shallow ribs with neat white small radial spines. 1 points to a complete finger-like main stem; 2 to a shallow rib; 3 to a small areole bearing short spines; 4 to a tiny new basal offset. No flowers because cultivar is unknown.

lookalikes.name: Golden ball cactus
lookalikes.text: Parodia leninghausii develops a denser golden coat and an upright column; peanut hybrids spread as many fingerlike stems.

mature.text: Expect a low, spreading clump rather than a tall column. The ancestor's dimensions are not a reliable size limit for an unidentified hybrid.

milestones.text: Purchased at Carlsons' Greenhouse in a 4-inch individual pot.

nameStory.text: The familiar peanut shape belongs to a species now listed by Kew as Echinopsis chamaecereus; Chamaecereus survives widely in horticultural hybrid names.
